## Deadlines and Late Work {.unnumbered}

Canvas lists every due date.

- Homework is due Friday at 10pm,
  with no-penalty extensions until Sunday at 10pm.
  I will not be available for help on weekends.
- The last homework, Homework 6, is due before finals week and has no extension.
- Lab deliverables are due as described under [Labs](#labs).

Please talk to me *in advance* if you need an accommodation or an extension;
the day an assignment is due is too late.
If you miss a deadline or an exam because of a medical emergency,
contact me as soon as possible to discuss arrangements.

## Collaboration and AI Tools {.unnumbered}

**Collaboration.**
You may work together on homework and worksheets
unless an assignment or problem says it is individual.
A group of about three works best,
since it is hard for everyone to contribute in a large group.
You may discuss the steps of an algorithm or proof on a whiteboard,
but write your own math and code,
and submit your own answers.
Do not copy from classmates, the internet, a chatbot, or a forum.

**AI tools.**
AI tools such as large language model chatbots
are **allowed on homework and worksheets only**.
Use them like a collaborator, not as a source of answers:
you must still write your answer in your own words,
and you are responsible for understanding it.
**Say whether you used an AI tool, and name it,** on each assignment.
Students who rely heavily on AI tools often struggle on exams,
where the tools are not available.
AI tools are not allowed on lab work,
including lab work you finish after the lab period.

**Exams** are solo:
work alone, without help from anyone else and without AI tools;
the only aid allowed is the note sheet handed out with the exam, as described under [Exams](#exams).

## Academic Honesty {.unnumbered}

As a future professional, your integrity is crucial.
It is your responsibility to read and be familiar with the university's academic honesty policy,
found in [Appendix D](https://catalog.wwu.edu/content.php?catoid=19&navoid=5073)
of the Western Washington University Course Catalog;
[Academic Honesty Resources for Students](https://academichonesty.wwu.edu/)
explains the procedures and the appeal process.
Cheating on an exam will result in failing the course (grade of F),
and I will file documentation of the incident with the university.
All cases of academic dishonesty will be reported.
When in doubt, ask me.
